habitat: Pairs or small groups along fast-running forest rivers and streams in the eastern regions. It hops from boulder to boulder and wags its tail.
summary: A fairly common, localised resident. A very long tail, white below with a narrow black breast-band, and mostly grey and white. Much paler than the other wagtails. The call on taking flight is chirrup, and the song is ti-tuu-ui-tui-tui. The Kemp paper name Longtailed Wagtail and the code NB were left unchanged.

calls.description: Chirrup on taking flight. It also sings ti-tuu-ui-tui-tui. Grade A call from the upper Kariega River, Eastern Cape. The filename is XC490751-Mountain Wagtail (3).mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common, localised resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Population figures, the paper name Longtailed Wagtail and the Kemp code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Cape Wagtail is shorter-tailed and greyer, and its breast-band is usually broader. Mountain Wagtail is much paler.
